From: Wildlife abundance estimation using distance sampling techniques. =
on behalf of Len Thomas
Sent: Mon 8/30/2010 9:58 PM

Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] creating a Coverage layer for DSM



Also, double-check the projection and the units you're using to specify
the spacing. - len

On 30/08/2010 11:37, Eric Rexstad wrote:
> > Chandra:
> >
> > Look at the Properties associated by default with the Coverage layer =
you
> > are trying to create. There will be a default spacing of the grid
> > points. Distance is reporting that the spacing is too coarse for any
> > points to fit within the specified (by the shape file) study region
> > boundary.
> >
> > Specifying the spacing is an iterative process in Distance; recall you
> > are essentially going to overwrite the coverage layer that you are
> > asking Distance to manufacture by the prediction grid that you have
> > constructed with your GIS. If my advice confuses you even further, =
send
> > your project along to me, and I can have a look next week (after we
> > finish our workshops here in St. Andrews).
> >
> > Chandra Salgado Kent wrote:
>> >> Hello,
>> >>
>> >> Just wondering if someone can help me with importing GIS information
>> >> into Distance 6.0. When I attempt to create a Coverage layer (for
>> >> Density Surface Modelling) I receive a message which says "The new =
layer
>> >> will have approximately 0 grid points in it, Do you want to =
continue?".
>> >> If I click "yes", I receive a message saying that "No grid points =
fell
>> >> inside the survey area".
>> >> I have checked to see if the grid points fall within the survey area,
>> >> and according to ArcGIS 9.2 they do. I have checked that the =
coordinate
>> >> system is the same as the global coordinate system, and they are (and =
I
>> >> switched the global coordinate system off within Distance before
>> >> attempting to create the Coverage layer). Any ideas or pointers would =
be
>> >> very helpful!
>> >>
>> >> Many thanks in advance!
>> >>
>> >> Chandra Salgado
